body:
The statement limit is now always decremented when using an iterator, in 7.11 notice the `IINC 1 -1`.
```
    INVOKEINTERFACE java/util/Iterator.next ()Ljava/lang/Object; (itf)
    ASTORE 19
    IINC 1 -1
    ILOAD 1
    ICONST_0
    IF_ICMPGT L37
    NEW org/elasticsearch/painless/PainlessError
    DUP
    LDC "The maximum number of statements that can be executed in a loop has been reached."
    INVOKESPECIAL org/elasticsearch/painless/PainlessError.<init> (Ljava/lang/String;)V
    ATHROW
```

Whereas in 7.9 iterators didn't decrement the limit on `Iterator.next()`, notice `IINC 1 0`
```
    INVOKEINTERFACE java/util/Iterator.next ()Ljava/lang/Object; (itf)
    ASTORE 19
    IINC 1 0
    ILOAD 1
    ICONST_0
    IF_ICMPGT L36
    NEW org/elasticsearch/painless/PainlessError
    DUP
    LDC "The maximum number of statements that can be executed in a loop has been reached."
    INVOKESPECIAL org/elasticsearch/painless/PainlessError.<init> (Ljava/lang/String;)V
```

Looking at the code, this appears to also be an issue with arrays.

Loop counter changed in the following:
```def x = []; for (y in x) { int z; }```
```List x = []; for (y in x) { int z; }```
```int[] x = new int[] {}; for (y in x) { int z; }```

issue.title: Remove loop counter for foreach loops

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body: This changes remove the loop counter for for each loops which is a regression from 7.9.3 documented in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/71584. Not loop counting for each loops should be relatively safe as they have a natural ending point. We can consider adding the check back in once we have configurable loop counters.
